## Description

When a ClusterQueue is configured with multiple TAS ResourceFlavors and flavorFungibility.whenCanPreempt is TryNextFlavor, a flavor that fits quota but requires preemption in TAS was bypassing fallback to subsequent flavors, preempting lower-priority workloads even when alternative flavors had idle quota and topology.

Record TAS placement downgrades in TASFlavorModes during topology assignment and retry flavor selection with capped preemption modes, allowing TryNextFlavor to evaluate subsequent candidate flavors within the same planning cycle.

#### What this PR does / why we need it?

<!--
Use `Fixes #123` for an issue addressed by this PR; it will be closed when the PR merges.
Use `Related:` or `Part of:` to reference an issue without closing it.
-->
Fixes #17396

When a ClusterQueue is configured with multiple TAS ResourceFlavors and `flavorFungibility.whenCanPreempt: TryNextFlavor`, a flavor that fits quota but requires preemption in TAS was bypassing fallback to subsequent candidate flavors. This resulted in premature preemption of lower-priority workloads even when alternative flavors had both idle quota and topology available.

This occurred because `AssignFlavors` selects the first candidate solely based on quota (`Fit`). When `AssignTopology` later discovered that physical node domains require preemption, it downgraded the mode to `Preempt`, but planning immediately proceeded to victim preemption without re-evaluating `TryNextFlavor`.

This PR introduces same-cycle TAS flavor retry:
1. Records TAS placement downgrades in `TASFlavorModes` during topology assignment.
2. Retries flavor selection with capped preemption modes, allowing `shouldTryNextFlavor()` to evaluate subsequent flavors when `whenCanPreempt: TryNextFlavor` is enabled.
3. Bounds the retry loop by total flavor count across resource groups, with convergence detection (`flavorsEqual`).
4. Adds unit test `TestPlan_TASWhenCanPreemptTryNextFlavor` verifying fallback without preemption.

## AI summary

This PR changes how Kueue selects a flavor for TAS (Topology Aware Scheduling) workloads when a ClusterQueue has multiple ResourceFlavors and `flavorFungibility.whenCanPreempt` is `TryNextFlavor`.

Before this change, Kueue could select a flavor that fit by quota but needed preemption for topology placement. Kueue then preempted a lower-priority workload on that flavor in the same scheduling cycle. It did not evaluate later flavors that could admit the workload without preemption.

After this change:

- TAS placement records a downgrade from `Fit` to `Preempt` (or to `NoFit`) per PodSet topology group and flavor.
- When `TryNextFlavor` is set, planning retries flavor selection in the same cycle with the recorded TAS modes. The retry loop is bounded and stops when flavor assignments converge.
- Planning uses the next flavor that can admit the workload without preemption, when one exists.
- With `MayStopSearch`, planning keeps the first flavor and preempts its victim, as before.
- The integration test for preserved flavor scan progress no longer waits for a TAS placement failure warning event. The pending workload is admitted on flavor 1 instead.

The new `TASFlavorModes` type, `TASMode`, and `TASFlavorKey` are internal scheduler types. The PR adds unit and scheduler tests for this behavior.

### Suggested release note

```text
TAS: Fixed a bug where a Workload that fit the quota of a ResourceFlavor but required preemption for topology placement could preempt a lower-priority Workload, even when a later ResourceFlavor could admit it without preemption. This behavior applies when `flavorFungibility.whenCanPreempt` is set to `TryNextFlavor`. Now Kueue tries the later ResourceFlavor in the same scheduling cycle before it preempts.
```

Rationale: The `TAS:` prefix is the narrowest accurate scope. The change affects TAS flavor selection. The note states the broken scenario, the bad user-visible effect (unneeded preemption), and the corrected behavior. It does not describe the implementation. No breaking change or `ACTION REQUIRED` mitigation applies. No feature gate is named in the evidence available, so none is mentioned.

### Comment by [@mishradwaterlaw](https://github.com/mishradwaterlaw) — 2026-10-22T06:44:43Z

cc @j-skiba 

I have implemented the same-cycle retry mechanism to address #17396:

1. When a flavor fits quota (`Fit`) but fails TAS placement with preemption needed (`Preempt`), `AssignTopologyWithModes` records the downgrade in `TASFlavorModes`.
2. Planning retries flavor selection with `tasModes` in effect. `findFlavorForPodSets` caps the flavor mode so `shouldTryNextFlavor()` evaluates alternative flavors when `flavorFungibility.whenCanPreempt: TryNextFlavor` is enabled.
3. Added `TestPlan_TASWhenCanPreemptTryNextFlavor` verifying that fallback without preemption occurs when the first flavor requires TAS preemption.

so i had a  question regarding `TestScheduleForPreserveFlavorScanProgress`:

while verifying the scheduler tests, I noticed an interaction with `TestScheduleForPreserveFlavorScanProgress` (`pkg/scheduler/scheduler_preserve_flavor_scan_progress_test.go`). 

In `gate_disabled`, the test previously expected `wantPendingFlavor: ""`. That test assumed that within a single scheduling cycle, a workload could never evaluate the second flavor when the first fit quota, so without `FlavorFungibilityPreserveScanProgress` it stayed unadmitted across cycles under churn.

With same-cycle retry under `whenCanPreempt: TryNextFlavor`, Kueue now recognizes that `tas-flavor-1` requires preemption, evaluates `tas-flavor-2` in the same cycle, and admits the workload immediately on `tas-flavor-2`. 

In this PR, I updated the expectation for `gate_disabled` to `"tas-flavor-2"` to reflect this immediate admission. Could you please confirm if this update aligns with your expectations, or if you prefer that `TestScheduleForPreserveFlavorScanProgress`'s ClusterQueue explicitly configure `whenCanPreempt: MayStopSearch` when isolating the cross-cycle preservation gate?

### Comment by [@mishradwaterlaw](https://github.com/mishradwaterlaw) — 2026-11-13T15:47:42Z

hi @apullo777 since TryNextFlavor is the existing default and the previous behavior preempting when an alternative flavor has idle topology  is strictly worse than what the API semantics promise, I'd treat this as a correctness bug fix rather than a behavior change. No feature gate needed. Users who explicitly chose TryNextFlavor already opted into this semantics. If we ever need to gate the same-cycle retry specifically (e.g., for performance-sensitive paths), the existing FlavorFungibility gate already guards the whole fungibility path; we can narrow it then. Happy to add a gate if the approvers feel differently.

+		}

  <!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->
  
  **🎯 Functional Correctness** | **🟠 Major** | **⚡ Quick win**
  
  **Complete topology assignment when the retry loop runs out of attempts.**
  
  Each non-final iteration ends with the assignment re-run through `AssignTopologyWithModes`. On the last iteration the loop can still request a retry, call `AssignFlavorsWithTASModes`, and get a different assignment. The loop then exits and only logs. That assignment never runs topology assignment.
  
  If the last reassigned assignment is `Fit`, `Plan` skips `updateAssignmentForTAS`, which only handles `Preempt`. The workload can then be admitted with no `TopologyAssignment`.
  
  `maxAttempts` is `flavorCount+1`, but a downgrade key is per (PodSet group, flavor). Several PodSet groups, or a preempt-then-noFit downgrade on one flavor, can record more downgrades than `maxAttempts` allows. The loop can then end on a reassigned `Fit` assignment that was never placed.
  
  Run topology assignment to completion with nil modes after the loop. Alternatively, pass nil modes on the final attempt.
  
  <details>
  <summary>🐛 Proposed fix</summary>
  
  ```diff
  --- "a/pkg/scheduler/assignment/native/native.go"
  +++ "b/pkg/scheduler/assignment/native/native.go"
  @@ -137,8 +137,11 @@
   			return
   		}
   	}
   	log.V(2).Info("TAS flavor retry loop reached maximum attempts", "maxAttempts", maxAttempts)
  +	// The last reassigned assignment has not been through topology assignment yet.
  +	// Complete it without a retry signal so TAS placement or failure is resolved.
  +	p.assigner.AssignTopologyWithModes(ctx, log, asgn, nil)
   }
   
   func flavorsEqual(a, b *flavorassigner.Assignment) bool {
   	if a == nil || b == nil || len(a.PodSets) != len(b.PodSets) {
  ```
  </details>

### Review by [@apullo777](https://github.com/apullo777) (commented) — 2026-10-28T07:05:02Z

Thanks! A couple of things I noticed while testing:

1. The failing TAS integration spec (`should fall back to preemption on the first flavor...`) still expects a `TopologyPlacementFailed` event for flavor 2, which is no longer emitted with same-cycle retry. Could we update the expectation while preserving its fallback coverage?
2. Could we also cover a few boundary cases? The simulated-empty fallback, the `MayStopSearch` no-retry path, and the reverse of the new test—when the alternative flavor doesn't work out, we should still retain the original preemption targets. I confirmed the last one works locally.

One other thought on rollout: since `TryNextFlavor` is the default, this will affect existing multi-flavor TAS queues too. WDYT about a feature gate, similar to `FlavorFungibilityPreserveScanProgress`, or is this reasonable to ship as a bug fix without one?

  **Complete the mode downgrade before declaring convergence.**
  
  If flavor A fits quota but cannot fit topology even when empty, the first failure caps A at `preempt`. If flavor B requires quota preemption, both candidates can now have equal mode and borrowing level. Flavor selection retains A.
  
  This branch then restores A and completes topology assignment with nil modes. A becomes `NoFit`, but planning never tries the viable preemption path on B.
  
  Run the capped assignment through the simulated-empty check with `tasModes` before treating unchanged flavor names as convergence. This permits the required `preempt`-to-`noFit` downgrade and another flavor selection.
